chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Ibn Abi Najran, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibrahim and al-Fadl, the two sons of Muhammad al-Ash'ariyyin, from Ubayd ibn Zurarah, from his father, who said: I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'May I be your ransom! What is the swooning that used to afflict the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) when revelation was sent down to him?'

He (peace be upon him) answered: 'That is when there is no one between him and Allah, that is when Allah manifests Himself to him.' He said: Then he (peace be upon him) added: 'That is prophethood, O Zurarah! Accept it with humility.'

key_terms.الغَشْيَة: Swooning or fainting, a state of losing consciousness due to intense divine presence
key_terms.الوَحْي: Revelation, the divine message sent to prophets

ai.seo_question: What is the theological explanation for the Prophet's swooning during revelation in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid* elucidates the doctrine of *Nazar* (vision) by distinguishing the Prophet Muhammad’s direct, unmediated encounter with the Divine Essence from the general prophetic experience. It highlights the unique ontological status of the Prophet, where the veil of intermediaries was lifted, allowing for a direct manifestation of Allah, a concept central to Shia theological debates on divine visibility. The instruction to 'accept with humility' underscores the epistemological weight of this direct experience, linking it to the broader Shia understanding of the Prophet’s infallible reception of revelation.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 15. My father (rh) said: Sa`d ibn `Abdillah said on the authority of Ibrahim ibn Hashim, on the authority of the Ibn Abu Najran, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sinan, on the authority of Ibrahim and al-Fadl sons of Muhammad al-Ash`ariyyayn, on the authority of Ubayd ibn Zurarah, on the authority of his father that I asked Abu `Abdillah (AS): “May I be your ransom! What used to make the Messenger of Allah (sw) swoon when he received the revelation?”

He (AS) answered: “That happened when there was no one between him and Allah. That happened when Allah manifested Himself to him.” He says that he (AS) then added: “Such is prophethood, O Zurarah! Accept it with humility.”
